seen_animation: A black-line mermaid lies tilted on her back across the middle of a grey scene (zigzag ceiling, a rock pillar on the left, a tree on the right, a ground line beneath her). Her body, hair strokes and forked tail stay fixed in place for the whole shot; only one arm moves. In frames 1-4 the arm is bent up beside the head and a long thin line runs right from the head, as if she holds something up. In frames 5-8 the arm straightens and points forward to the right. In frames 9-10 it folds back so the hand comes to the face as a narrow V over the head. In frames 11-12 the arm is raised upward from the head. In frames 13-16 it extends forward to the right again.
seen_film: A mermaid with long hair and a large scaled tail curled at the end reclines in an underwater grotto, body and tail held still in the centre of the frame. In frames 1-3 she holds a string (of pearls) up near her head with her raised arm. In frames 4-6 she lowers the string and extends her arm forward to the right. In frames 7-10 she brings the hand back to her face and hair. In frames 11-12 she raises the arm up above her shoulder. In frames 13-16 she stretches the arm out forward to the right again.
named_subject: A reclining mermaid moving one arm (holding up a string, reaching forward, touching her face, raising the arm, reaching forward again).
evidence: The arm-only action matches the film beat for beat at the same moments, with the body held still as in the film: e.png 1-4 arm raised beside the head with a long line running right (film 1-4 holds the pearl string up); e.png 5-12 the arm swings out and straightens forward-right (film 5-12 reaches forward); e.png 13-24 the arm folds back to the face as a V over the head (film 15-26 hand at face); e.png 25-29 the forearm stands vertical above the head (film 27-30 arm raised); e.png 30-38 the arm extends forward-right again (film 31-38). g.png shows no body travel, only motion clustered at the head, which matches the film where only the arm moves. Small pops: e.png 4 to 5 the long held line shortens abruptly; e.png 12 to 13 the straight forearm becomes a short vertical hook in one frame; e.png 24 to 25 the V over the face becomes an upright bent arm in one frame. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: In e.png 13-24 the hand-to-face pose is drawn as a thin closed V sliver lying across the head and hair strokes, so it reads as a scribble on the face rather than an arm bent up with the hand at the cheek.
closes_when: In e.png 13-24 the arm is drawn as a separate bent limb whose elbow sits clearly out from the body on the right of the head and whose hand ends at the side of the face, without overlapping the hair strokes.
protect: The doodle's body, hair strokes, waist band and forked tail kept unchanged and fixed in place as in the film; the single moving arm; the timing of the five arm beats (hold string, reach, hand to face, raise, reach) matched to the film's frames; the stroke weight and plain closed-outline style of c.png.
identity_gap: The body, hair lines and tail are the c.png drawing tilted back to recline, and the added arm uses the same thin outline habit, though in the face-touch frames it tangles with the hair strokes.
